interviewQuestions.question: Design the news feed ranking system for a social app.
interviewQuestions.answerMarkdown:
I'd start by clarifying scale and latency — assume hundreds of millions of daily feed loads, sub-300ms end-to-end. That immediately implies a multi-stage funnel rather than one model scoring everything.

**Candidate generation**: pull a few hundred posts per user from people/pages they follow plus a recommended pool, using a cheap retrieval method so it's feasible per-request at this scale.

**Ranking**: score that shortlist with a model using user, content, and — most valuable — cross features (this user's history with this specific author/topic). I wouldn't train on a single label; I'd predict several engagement proxies (like, comment, share, watch-time) and combine them, since any single proxy alone gets gamed or misrepresents true value — raw engagement optimization specifically breeds outrage-bait.

**Re-ranking**: apply freshness decay and diversity caps (no more than 2 consecutive posts from one author) as an explicit rule layer on top of the relevance score, since that's easier to tune than teaching a model the property implicitly.

I'd close on evaluation and monitoring: offline NDCG/precision@k as a cheap filter, then an A/B test on retention and meaningful-interaction rate — not just engagement — before shipping, plus drift monitoring since content and user behavior both shift over time.

**Testing:** whether you can integrate ranking, label design, and business-rule layering into one coherent answer instead of only naming a model.
